paper_title: A Pyrene-Fused Dimerized Acceptor for Ternary Organic Solar Cells with 19% Efficiency and High Thermal Stability

knowledge_points.content: DP-BTP is a novel 'center-fused' dimerized electron acceptor featuring a 'butterfly-like' structure where two Y-series acceptor wings are fused to a central pyrene-based backbone.
knowledge_points.evidence: This novel electron acceptor displays a distinctive 'butterflylike' structure, comprising two Y-acceptors as wings fused with a pyrene-based backbone... denoted as DP-BTP (Figure 1b), has been synthesized and applied into OSCs.

knowledge_points.content: The synthesis of the pyrene-fused core M3 is achieved through a high-yielding (66%) dehydration reaction between a diamine-substituted precursor (M1) and 4,5,9,10-pyrenetetrone (M2).
knowledge_points.evidence: the pyrene-fused core, denoted as M3, was initially formed through a high-yielding (66%) dehydration reaction between the precursor M1, and tetrone compounds M2.

knowledge_points.content: Ternary organic solar cells using the D18:N3:DP-BTP blend achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.07%, with an open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 0.87 V, a short-circuit current density (Jsc) of 27.95 mA/cm², and a fill factor (FF) of 78.50%.
knowledge_points.evidence: the ternary D18: N3:DP-BTP (1 : 0.9 : 0.4, w/w) system exhibited a remarkable PCE of 19.07%. This is attributed to the simultaneously enhanced Voc of 0.87 V, Jsc of 27.95 mA/cm2 and FF of 78.50% compared to the D18:N3 cells.

knowledge_points.content: The dimerized acceptor DP-BTP exhibits a significantly higher glass transition temperature (Tg) of 126 °C compared to the 88 °C observed for the small-molecule acceptor N3.
knowledge_points.evidence: the DP-BTP dimer exhibited a much higher Tg of 126 °C than that of N3 (88 °C).

knowledge_points.content: DP-BTP has a lower solubility in chloroform (1.60 mg/mL) compared to N3 (155.90 mg/mL), which is attributed to its highly planar molecular configuration and extended pi-conjugation.
knowledge_points.evidence: the acceptor N3 exhibited an excellent solubility of 155.90 mg/mL, while DPBTP exhibited a markedly lower solubility of 1.60 mg/mL which may be related to its highly planar molecular configuration.

knowledge_points.content: The inclusion of DP-BTP in ternary OSCs improves electron mobility (μe) from 4.18 × 10⁻³ cm²/(V·s) in binary D18:N3 cells to 5.20 × 10⁻³ cm²/(V·s), leading to a more balanced hole/electron mobility ratio of 1.17.
knowledge_points.evidence: the electron mobility (μe) of D18:N3 measured at 4.18 × 10−3 cm2/(V s) saw an increase to 5.20 × 10−3 cm2/(V s) upon the incorporation of DP-BTP... the μh/μe ratio exhibited a more balanced distribution in D18:N3:DP-BTP ternary blends (1.17) compared to the D18:N3 binary system (1.45).

knowledge_points.content: DP-BTP reduces non-radiative voltage loss (ΔVnr) in OSCs, which is attributed to the high fluorescence emission efficiency of the pyrene unit within the dimer structure.
knowledge_points.evidence: the pyrene-fused dimerized electron acceptor DP-BTP effectively mitigates both radiative and non-radiative voltage losses in OSCs. This would be attributed to the high fluorescence emission efficiency of pyrene units

knowledge_points.content: The Flory-Huggins interaction parameter (χ) between N3 and DP-BTP is calculated at 0.34k, indicating high miscibility and the formation of alloy-like acceptor domains in the ternary blend.
knowledge_points.evidence: N3 and DP-BTP exhibit better miscibility compared to D18/N3 or D18/DP-BTP pairs, as indicated by the substantially smaller χ parameter of 0.34k... we propose a plausible alloy-packing structure of N3 and DP-BTP

knowledge_points.content: Ternary OSCs based on D18:N3:DP-BTP retain 88.7% of their initial efficiency after 600 hours of thermal stress at 80 °C, significantly outperforming binary D18:N3 cells which retain only 73.7%.
knowledge_points.evidence: After constant... heat exposure for 600 hours, the binary OsC maintained... 73.7% of their initial PCEs... the incorporation of DP-BTP... maintained... 88.7% of PCEs maintained under... thermal-stress conditions

knowledge_points.content: The photostability of D18:N3:DP-BTP ternary devices is enhanced compared to binary systems, retaining 86.9% of initial PCE after 600 hours of continuous LED illumination, with a calculated T80 lifetime of 4963 hours.
knowledge_points.evidence: After constant illumination... for 600 hours, the binary OsC maintained 64.8%... The incorporation of DP-BTP... with 86.9%... maintained... The calculated T80 lifetimes... for the ternary blends are 4963... hours for OsCs under photo-stress

knowledge_points.content: Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations indicate that DP-BTP possesses a highly planar configuration, with the LUMO localized on the Y-acceptor wings and the HOMO delocalized over the central pyrene core.
knowledge_points.evidence: DFT calculations revealed a highly planar configuration for DP-BTP (Figure 2b), with the lowest unoccupied molecular orbitals (LUMO) localized at the two 'y' wings and the highest occupied molecular orbitals (HOMO) delocalized over the central core

knowledge_points.content: GIWAXS analysis reveals that D18:N3:DP-BTP ternary films maintain a face-on preferential orientation with a pi-pi (010) stacking peak at q ≈ 1.73 Å⁻¹.
knowledge_points.evidence: in D18:N3:DP-BTP ternary blends, the measured (100) and (010) peaks were observed at q = 0.30 Å−1 and 1.73 Å−1... face-on preferential orientation, as evidenced by the... OOP π-π (010) peaks.
